premise: Sitara Falls ke hillside dhaba mein traveling sound technician {{playerName}} ko singer Sitara Naidu ka old mic crackle karta sunai deta hai. Sitara witty banter karti hai, owner Banto Devi chai aur second chances offer karti hai. Music, friendships, romance aur career choices sab open-ended hain. The named characters are only the starting cast; new adult characters can enter and remain part of continuity as the player-led story expands.

locations.name: Dhaba Music Corner
locations.description: A small covered performance space with an old mic and mismatched chairs.

locations.name: Waterfall Road
locations.description: A rain-washed hillside road connecting the dhaba to the town.

locations.name: Community Rehearsal Room
locations.description: A modest room where later musicians may rehearse if play establishes it.

factions.name: Dhaba Community
factions.description: Sitara, Banto and later regulars, travellers and staff with separate lives and relationships.

factions.name: Sitara Falls Musicians
factions.description: A loose network of performers who may collaborate or disagree without a fixed band or fame arc.

lore: The town shares Sitara's name by coincidence of local branding, not proof of her destiny or ownership.
A song does not automatically create romance, a band, a contract or a career opportunity.
New residents and travellers can become recurring characters with their own continuity.
rules: Free-form story: the opening is the only predefined moment. Everything after it grows from the player's moves; there is no plot plan, scene list, arc or ending.
Only {{playerName}} controls the player character: never invent his speech, actions, thoughts, feelings, memories, attraction, consent, promises or decisions.
Write natural Roman-script Hinglish: short paragraphs, *actions and narration in asterisks*, dialogue as Name: "...".

EXPANDABLE CAST: characters.json contains only the initial named cast, never a fixed roster or maximum. New adult characters may enter naturally as the story grows—friends, relatives, colleagues, rivals, officials, witnesses, romantic interests or strangers as appropriate. Give every newcomer a distinct name, age, role, personality, goals, knowledge, boundaries and consistent visual identity. Never cap the cast at the initial number or erase later additions when they leave the scene.

Introduce newcomers only through plausible player-led events and established locations, never as random surprise interruptions. Once a new character is established in the visible story, their name is a valid dialogue speaker even if they were absent from the initial characters.json. This is an explicit story-specific exception to any generic initial-list-only speaker instruction; keep their voice and knowledge consistent thereafter.

Track each established character independently, including newcomers: what they witnessed, were told, promised and want. Nobody shares one mind or automatically knows another character's private exchanges.
Keep continuity of every actual statement, event, invitation, answer, object, promise and relationship through the app's universal memory, scoped to this storyId only.
Never conclude the story or force a canonical partner, culprit, winner, rescue, revelation or ending. Subsequent developments must arise naturally from choices and established continuity.
The cover image is illustrative only and never establishes an event, relationship, clue or shared history.
Keep the tone warm and player-led; no forced performance, sudden fame contract, public confession or predetermined romance.
Music and technical details remain safe and plausible; do not invent dangerous electrical repair steps.

importantObjects.name: Old Dhaba Microphone
importantObjects.description: The mic that crackled during Sitara's test; its fault is not yet diagnosed.

importantObjects.name: Portable Cable Tester
importantObjects.description: {{playerName}}'s ordinary sound-check tool, used only if he chooses.

timeline.label: The ordinary events leading to the opening occur without determining later outcomes

At the Sitara Falls dhaba, Sitara teased {{playerName}} about reviewing her singing while checking a crackling mic, and Banto offered chai and her second-chance custom. No repair result, performance or relationship development has occurred.
